items.q: How does the AI video clipper choose moments?
items.a: Scribix uses the spoken content and timing to suggest moments with a clear theme and enough context to stand on their own. Review the suggestions and choose what you want to share.

items.q: Can I still use Scribix only for transcription?

Features.label: Features
Features.h2: Built for <accent>video creators</accent> who care about accuracy.
Features.intro: A video-to-text converter transcribes the spoken audio inside a video into written text. Modern AI speech models identify words, separate speakers, and attach timestamps — producing an editable transcript in minutes instead of hours. Scribix runs the same class of speech model that powers professional transcription suites — sign in with Google to get started and produce output clean enough to publish.

items.title: Speaker labels for conversations
items.body: Scribix requests speaker diarization during transcription and separates turns when the recording quality supports it. Labels can be renamed afterward.

items.title: Automatic language detection

items.title: Word-level timestamps

items.title: Five export formats

items.title: Reviewable transcript output
items.body: Results vary with recording quality, noise, accents, vocabulary, and overlapping speech. Speaker labels and timestamps make review faster.

items.q: Is Scribix really free for video to text?
items.a: Yes. Google sign-in gives you {freeTrialMinutes} lifetime transcription minutes with no credit card. Paid plans add monthly transcription minutes, AI notes, translation, and larger video uploads.

items.q: What video formats does Scribix support?
items.a: MP4, MOV, AVI, MKV, WebM, MP3, WAV, and M4A are supported. Free allows video up to 2 GB and audio up to 1 GB; paid plans allow video up to 5 GB and audio up to 1 GB, subject to duration and quota limits.

items.q: How accurate is Scribix's video-to-text?
items.a: Transcript quality depends on recording clarity, microphone distance, background noise, accents, specialized vocabulary, and overlapping speech. Review important transcripts before publishing or relying on them.

items.q: How many languages does Scribix support?
items.a: Scribix detects the spoken language automatically. Language coverage depends on the transcription model selected for your plan and the audio itself.

items.q: Can Scribix tell different speakers apart?
items.a: Yes. Scribix requests speaker labels during transcription, so conversations can be separated by speaker when recording quality supports it. You can rename the generated speaker labels afterward.

items.q: How long does video-to-text transcription take?
items.a: Processing time varies with file length, format, extraction needs, network conditions, and transcription-service load. Scribix shows progress while the job is running.

items.q: Is my data secure when I upload a video?
items.a: Original video retention depends on your plan and is shown before upload. Audio follows the standard source-file retention period. Transcripts remain until you delete them or close your account.

items.q: What can I export the transcript as?
items.a: Five formats: TXT (plain), DOCX (Word), SRT (subtitles), VTT (web subtitles), and CSV (spreadsheet-friendly). Click-to-edit inline before exporting.

items.q: Does Scribix work for podcasts and audio-only files?
items.a: Yes — but for an audio-first workflow, our dedicated audio-to-text tool is purpose-built for that intent. Same engine, same accuracy, audio-tuned UI.

quickAnswer.title: Paste a link. Save the captions.
quickAnswer.body: Scribix is a YouTube-to-transcript tool for turning available YouTube captions into a saved transcript. It is best for lectures, interviews, tutorials, webinars, podcasts, and research videos that already have manual or auto-generated captions. If a video has no captions, use the regular upload flow with your own audio or video file instead.

items.q: How do I turn a YouTube video into a transcript?
items.a: Paste the YouTube URL into Scribix, check the available caption tracks, choose a language, and import the transcript. Scribix saves the transcript to your account so you can review, copy, export, or summarize it on a paid plan.

items.q: Does Scribix work with every YouTube video?
items.a: No. The YouTube URL workflow works when Scribix can access at least one caption track for the video. If the video has no captions, is private, restricted, deleted, or blocked, Scribix may not be able to import a transcript.

items.q: Does Scribix download the YouTube video or audio?
items.a: No. Scribix imports available YouTube captions. It does not download the YouTube video or audio for this workflow.

items.q: Can Scribix generate a transcript if a YouTube video has no captions?
items.a: Not from the YouTube URL alone. If you own the media file, use Scribix's video-to-text or audio-to-text upload flow to generate a new AI transcript from the file.

items.q: Is YouTube to transcript free in Scribix?
items.a: Yes. Scribix includes 10 YouTube caption imports per day on the free plan with Google sign-in and no credit card.

items.q: What can I export the YouTube transcript as?
items.a: Scribix can export completed transcripts as TXT, DOCX, SRT, VTT, or CSV. You can also copy transcript text directly from the app.

items.q: Can I choose the transcript language?
items.a: Yes, when the YouTube video has multiple caption tracks. Scribix shows the available caption languages and lets you choose which one to import.

items.q: Can I summarize a YouTube transcript?
items.a: Yes. Paid users can use AI summaries after importing the YouTube transcript into Scribix.

items.q: Are imported YouTube transcripts accurate?
items.a: They are as accurate as the selected YouTube caption track. Manual captions are usually stronger than auto-generated captions, but every transcript should be reviewed before quoting, publishing, or using it for high-stakes decisions.

types.question: What types of videos work best?
types.answer: Start with speech-led recordings: podcasts, interviews, webinars, lessons, and talking-head videos. Clear audio and self-contained ideas give you useful moments to work with. Review clips that depend on slides, demonstrations, or visual context before exporting.

editing.question: Can I edit the clips selected by AI?
editing.answer: Yes. Paid plans let you adjust clip boundaries, correct subtitle text, change caption styling, and refine framing. Free users can review and export the original AI-suggested clips. Check every clip for meaning and caption accuracy before sharing.

count.question: How many clips will I get from one video?
count.answer: There is no fixed number. Suggestions depend on the material and the moments that can stand on their own. A video may produce several candidates, a few, or none. Review the suggestions and choose the ones that serve your audience.

youtube.question: Can I upload a YouTube link?
youtube.answer: For this clipping workflow, upload a video file from your device. Importing a YouTube URL as the source video is not currently supported. Scribix’s separate YouTube transcript tool imports captions; it does not import the source footage for clipping.
